evidence.claim: Kaggle ranks a team by the better PRIVATE score of its (up to) 2 selected final submissions; if none are selected, the 2 best public submissions are used automatically.

Closed form (Clark 1961): E[max(X1,X2)] = E[X1] + E[D+], E[D+] = mu*Phi(mu/s) + s*phi(mu/s) for D = X2 - X1 ~ N(mu, s). This is exact for correlated normals, because only D matters. The hypothesis arithmetic checks out: mu 0.002, s 0.004 -> +0.0028. The premium over the best single final is at most 0.4*s (at mu = 0).
evidence.source: Clark, Oper. Res. 9(2):145-162 (1961); emunix.emich.edu/~aross15/q/papers/bounds_Emax.pdf; arXiv 0910.0115; scratchpad emax_calib.py

evidence.claim: Practitioners usually pair a 'safe' final with an 'aggressive' one, or pick finals from different model classes, so that one wrong class does not sink both.

Across 112 Kaggle competitions there is little adaptive overfitting when the public and private splits are i.i.d. Our split is by embryo (not i.i.d.), so here the embryo-shift term dominates the public-private gap, not the size of the public set.
evidence.source: Roelofs et al., A Meta-Analysis of Overfitting in Machine Learning, NeurIPS 2019 (https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/ee39e503b6bedf0c98c388b7e8589aca-Paper.pdf)

evidence.claim: Lab to public transfer for small components is ~0. On the 6 lab/public pairs (DivNet veto +0.0022 -> 0.000, leaf prune +0.0006 -> 0.000, DN insertion +0.0019 -> +0.001, hygiene +0.0011 -> -0.001, relink-off +0.0053 -> -0.002, axis flip +0.0214 -> -0.001) the slope through the origin is -0.06, and -0.26 on the 5 post-processing pairs, with residual sd 0.0008-0.0009. The one-change public deltas of probes 18-28 have sd 0.0011 and mean -0.0009. So the real sigma of private D is epistemic (embryo transfer), not something the lab can resample.
evidence.source: CONTEXT.md sections 11 and 14; python -m kaggle competitions submissions (3-decimal public scores); scratchpad emax_calib.py

The parity kernel exp46 is sha256-identical to exp39, and the duplicate exp36 submission scored the same 0.946. evidence.claim: E[D+] increases in BOTH mu and sigma. The hypothesis rule 'a component with P(D<0) > 0.3 goes to neither final' therefore contradicts its own objective: a mu ~ 0, high-sigma component (for example the edge filter if probe 29 ties) is the most valuable F2 addition (premium 0.4*sigma ~ +0.0012..+0.0020 at sigma 0.003-0.005), while its downside is covered by F1.
evidence.source: closed form; scratchpad emax_calib.py scenario table

evidence.claim: Winner's curse: choosing F2 as the max-public of k near-identical variants inflates its public score by E[max of k N(0,1)] * sd = 0.85 (k=3) and 1.17 (k=5) sd, i.e. ~+0.0013/+0.0017 at sd 0.0015. This supports the 'never pick F2 as max of near-copies' clause.
Probes 29 (exp49, edge filter) and 30 (exp50, drop-only) were still PENDING at 24 Sep ~15:50 UTC; exp48 = 0.948 is the best scored public submission.

implementation_notes: 1) Objective. The objective max E[max(X1,X2)] is correct. With F1 fixed, choose F2 to maximise E[D+] = mu*Phi(mu/s) + s*phi(mu/s), NOT mu and NOT P(D>0). Rank F2 candidates by E[D+]. Drop the hypothesis' 'P(D<0) > 0.3 -> neither final' exclusion: it removes exactly the high-variance, mu ~ 0 components that best-of-two rewards. Keep only one hard screen: public(F2) >= public(F1) - 0.003, which catches real negatives like Z-flip -0.009 and secondary swaps -0.007..-0.025. 2) Where sigma comes from. It is NOT lab resampling (degenerate: P(D<0) = 0 everywhere) and NOT run noise (our pipeline is deterministic: parity sha256, duplicate submission identical). It is embryo transfer. Prior per component c: mu_c = w*pub_c + (1-w)*k*lab_c, with k ~ 0.3 for network-independent rules and ~0 for rules that trust the in-sample edge net/detector (measured slope -0.06..-0.26 for small post-proc components), w ~ 0.7-0.8 (public is an unseen embryo, like private). sigma_c^2 = (1.5 * embryo heterogeneity)^2 + 0.0011^2 (public one-change sd floor) + 0.0004^2 (rounding). Embryo heterogeneity from the lab = |d_44b6 - d_6bba|/sqrt(2): ef 0.0017, stitch 0.0009, leaf prune 0.00035, DN insertion 0.0004. For components with big lab gains this should scale with |mu| (guess: sd >= 0.3*|lab mu| for in-sample-net components). 3) Pitfalls. (a) Private is the other embryo(s), ~71%; a one-embryo private set means the embryo term is large, so sigma is likely under-estimated rather than over. (b) Bundling several independent mu ~ 0 components in F2 increases sigma and so E[D+]; that is fine for F2, but never put an un-probed component in F1. (c) F1 must be public-proven by a scored submission of the EXACT file. The coordhead port (exp51) is not proven until probed, so F1 = exp48(+ef if it wins) and coordhead enters F1 only after its own probe >= F1. (d) Every final must be an already-scored submission. Kernel ~35 min plus scoring 3-6 h plus 5/day, and from 26 Sep only final-candidate probes: F2 candidates must be submitted by 28 Sep ~12:00 UTC so the public floor can be checked. (e) Tick both finals manually by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC; otherwise Kaggle auto-picks the 2 best public (two near-copies, premium ~+0.0002). (f) The multiplier-share screen (<30%) is sound: the edge filter's node ratio 0.99958 makes its multiplier share ~0.3%. (g) Public scores are 3-decimal only (CLI confirmed), so ties within 0.001 are unresolvable. 4) Decision table (E[D+] from emax_calib.py; the mu/sigma inputs are guesses). ef wins publicly (>= +0.004): ef goes in BOTH finals; F2 = F1 + stitch + division cap, premium ~+0.0003..+0.0008. ef ties (0.947-0.949): F1 = exp48, F2 = exp48 + ef (+stitch), premium ~+0.0012..+0.0020, the best case for this rule. ef loses (<= 0.945): F2 = F1 + stitch/div-cap, whose mu ~ 0, s ~ 0.002 gives ~+0.0008 (ef at mu -0.003 gives only +0.0005 and fails the floor if <= F1 - 0.003).
refined_change: FINAL-SELECTION RULE (desk rule, no pipeline change; execute by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC, all inputs are already-scored submissions). F1 = the public-proven stack: exp48 (0.948), upgraded to exp48 + edge filter if probe 29 >= exp39 + 0.003 (i.e. >= 0.950), and + coordhead only if its own probe on that base is not worse. F2 = F1 + the bundle of components that maximises E[D+] = mu*Phi(mu/s) + s*phi(mu/s), with mu and s from the transfer-calibrated prior (see the lab test), subject to: (i) the bundle's scored public >= F1 - 0.003; (ii) each component is per-embryo non-negative in the lab (44b6 and 6bba deltas >= 0) and J-driven (multiplier share < 30%); (iii) F2 differs from F1 by at least one component with sigma >= 0.0015 (no near-copies, never the max-public among >= 2 variants of the same bundle). Do NOT exclude components for P(D<0) > 0.3. Candidates in priority order: edge filter (if probe 29 is a tie), stitch st_p07, DaughterNet cap, leaf prune (already in exp48). Submit the F2 bundle once (one probe) by 28 Sep 12:00 UTC.
refined_lab_test: Replace the degenerate pseudo-private bootstrap with a TRANSFER-CALIBRATED desk computation. No replay runs; laptop python < 1 min, nice -n 19. Inputs: per-video confirmation CSVs (l5/l6_per_video_confirmation_*.csv) for per-embryo lab deltas d44, d6b; the scored public deltas of every candidate bundle (kaggle CLI); the 6-7 historical lab/public pairs. Steps: (1) Fit the transfer slope k and residual sd on the historical pairs (current: k -0.06..-0.26, resid 0.0009; re-fit after probes 29/30 add the first large-effect pair, ef +0.016 lab). (2) For each component c: mu_c = 0.75*pub_c + 0.25*k*lab_c; s_c = sqrt((1.5*|d44 - d6b|/sqrt2)^2 + (0.3*k_eff*|lab_c|)^2 + 0.0011^2 + 0.0004^2). (3) For each candidate F2 bundle (sum of components, correlation 0.5 between components as a guess), compute E[D+] in closed form and a 20k-draw Monte Carlo check. Also run a sensitivity sweep with s x {0.5, 1, 2}. (4) Choose the F2 with the largest E[D+] that meets the public floor and the per-embryo/J screens. SUCCESS: the chosen pair's E[D+] exceeds the best near-copy pair (s ~0.0005 -> +0.0002) by >= +0.0005 AND the ranking of the top F2 does not change under the s x0.5 / x2 sweep. If the premium is < +0.0005 under every scenario (likely when ef wins big and is in both finals), fall back to F2 = F1 + stitch + div-cap as the 'aggressive' final and do not spend extra probes on it. Optional sanity check with the existing per-video CSVs: per-embryo sign agreement (44b6 vs 6bba) for each component. It is already known (ef, stitch, leaf prune, DN all same-sign), so it adds no new information.
expected_gain: +0.0002..+0.0020 expected private score over auto-picking the two best public submissions, depending on probe 29: largest (+0.0012..+0.0020) if the edge filter TIES publicly (mu ~ 0, sigma 0.003-0.005 on the private embryo; sigma is a guess), ~+0.0003..+0.0008 if the filter wins big and sits in both finals. It also avoids the winner's-curse inflation (~+0.0013 public for a max-of-3 pick) that would mislead a max-public F2. Zero pipeline risk; costs at most one probe slot for the F2 bundle.
